ASVspoof2019-LA-eval-sample10k.note: Stratified random 10,000-utterance sample of the ASVspoof2019 LA eval partition (of 71,933 total; 1,032 bonafide / 8,968 spoof, same ratio as the full partition), attack algorithms A07-A19, none seen in training. Trained on: ASVspoof2019 LA train (25,380 rows) + ASVspoof2019 LA dev (24,844 rows) + Release In-The-Wild real-world genuine+cloned audio (31,779 rows) + MLAAD English subset (580 rows spanning 116 distinct modern TTS/voice-cloning architectures) + 3 demo clips with SYMMETRIC noise/reverb augmentation on both bonafide and spoof sides (240 rows), oversampled 50x. The symmetric augmentation (2026-09-05, see HANDOFF.md §10) fixed a real robustness gap found by the test suite: cloned-voice detection used to collapse under noise (99->18) even though the model was fine on clean audio, because noise augmentation had only ever been applied to bonafide clips. Now robust across clean/noise/reverb/compression (see artifacts/TEST_SUITE_REPORT.md Experiment C). All 3 demo clips verified working. Does NOT reliably catch a fresh XTTS-v2 clone of a genuinely new (never-seen-anywhere) reference voice -- see HANDOFF.md for the full investigation (4 different fix attempts, all documented, why this is a known field-wide limitation rather than a bug in this project).

ASVspoof2019-LA-eval-sample10k-baseline-.note: Original checkpoint before the 2026-09-05 retrain, trained only on ASVspoof2019 LA train + 3 unaugmented demo clips. Kept for the before/after comparison -- don't quote this one on its own, it's superseded by the entry above.
